suggestions.quote: a forecast of the times you will meet them again in person, recalculated whenever your plans change
suggestions.fix: This reads like an essay. Speak it as fragments, curious and dry: "A number over everyone's head. How many more times you'll meet them. In person. It updates when your plans do." Direction: curious, then amused on "You shrug."

suggestions.quote: You leave for your first job next month
suggestions.fix: Use the contraction and give it a direction: "You're leaving for your first job next month." Direction: hushed, matter-of-fact, said right after the counter flips. Say.yaml: "forty-two" for the 42.

suggestions.quote: it was never her clock, only your trains
suggestions.fix: This is the line that lands the turn, so it must be a complete thought, not a fragment: "It was never counting her. It was counting you." Direction: surprised, then warm. It also breaks the planted "It only counts down."

suggestions.quote: the Tail End arithmetic on in-person time left with parents
suggestions.fix: Keep the spoken version to one number, in short sentences, tied to her counter: "Say you go home four times a year. Then it's not years. It's visits. Thirty-seven of them." Direction: hushed. Give the visit rate and any large figures a say.yaml spoken form ("four hundred", "three thousand", "seven thousandths of a second" style).

suggestions.quote: She's still at the door. Of course she is.
suggestions.fix: No text change. It is close to narrating the picture, so keep "Of course she is" as the added wry beat, and attach the direction "low, warm, half-smiling". If the animator shows her at the door clearly, don't add any more narration before it.

suggestions.quote: mom keeps chai waiting at the door and packs food for the return train
suggestions.fix: The picture already shows these warm beats, so give them a spoken line that adds, not narrates. For example, "She packs enough for two trains." Direction: warm, amused.
